title: Disconnect an app
summary: Mara's confirmation for Disconnect on Diceroll's Connected apps row, open in the row: which devices sign out and when, that the game keeps playing because the license stays, what happens to Cloud Sync, and that the developer keeps only what it already received.
compare: 2026-10-20 shell (PX-35, BR-lockups): no header Activate (the account menu's first item); no footer (Help and Privacy are in the account menu); the docked Library · Discover phone bar, neither tab current; the trimmed Locker lockup. The page frame is the built Account's (PX-31a, as identity.connected-apps), with Packages in place of 'Access tokens'.

The confirmation moved from a dialog into the row, the built Account's one pattern for a removal (a sign-in method's Disconnect, a token's Revoke, Delete account: MethodRow, PackagesCard; baseline account-disconnect). The build wins: one way to confirm on the page. Build follow-up: build Disconnect this way when Connected apps lands (I-34, PX-31b).

Disconnect opens a danger panel under the row's chips; the row's own buttons give way while it is open. Focus moves to the panel's heading 'Disconnect Diceroll?'; Escape or Keep Diceroll closes it and returns focus to Disconnect.

The first line names every device that signs out (from the account's devices for this product) and when: the next time the game checks in, within an hour (the app session's refresh interval through I-11's revocation hook; use the server's real figure).

Bullets, one fact each: the game keeps playing on those devices; the license stays; Cloud Sync stops until the next sign-in (only for products with Cloud Sync); the saves stay; the developer keeps what it already received and gets nothing new. identity.sign-in-off describes devices the same way.
A muted line says the next sign-in asks what to share again (the grant is revoked, so consent shows again).

Buttons say what happens: 'Keep Diceroll' (outline, first) and the danger 'Disconnect Diceroll'. On success the row leaves the list, a toast says 'Diceroll is disconnected' and focus moves to the card's heading; its devices sign out through I-11's revocation hook (I-34 acceptance).
Never 'Revoke grant' or 'Deauthorize' in customer copy; the Locker verb is Disconnect.
Phone: the panel spans the row's text column, its two buttons full width, Keep first; 44 px targets.
Portal v2 (B2, B12): the docked header, row actions outlined, the page h1 at the display step (48/52, 32/36 on a phone) with no full stop or eyebrow, no glow or wash; weights 400/500/600.

designReview.reviewer: UX designer (visual critique of rendered screenshots)
designReview.verdict: Fixed: the dialog now says exactly what happens on Mara's devices, and it agrees with sign-in-off.

findings.issue: It didn't say whether Diceroll stops working on Mara's Pixel 8 and Steam Deck, and seemed to contradict sign-in-off's 'devices already activated keep working'.
findings.resolution: 'Diceroll is signed out on the 2 devices it's on, Mara's Pixel 8 and Steam Deck, the next time it checks in, within an hour.' First bullet: 'The game keeps playing on both. Your Diceroll Standard license stays activated there and stays in your library.' sign-in-off uses the same timing and the same device rule; Connected apps' footnote agrees.

findings.issue: '…already received, your screen name, and gets nothing new' read as a list; the compare said the header stays visible but it was blurred.
findings.resolution: 'Example Games keeps what it already received (your screen name) and gets nothing new.' The compare now says the whole page dims. The dialog is centred on desktop and a bottom sheet on phone, like the other identity dialogs.

findings.issue: Danger action the easiest tap; Cancel looked like a second primary in light.
findings.resolution: Phone sheet: Keep first, Disconnect second and outlined; Cancel is outline with no focus fill; bullets one clause; destructive label white in dark.
